title: Over a local ring whose etale algebras retract through rational points, a finite type algebra splits off a finite factor (Stacks 04GG (8)$\Rightarrow$(11))
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring such that for every ring map $R\to R'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every prime ideal $\mathfrak m'\subset R'$ lying over $\mathfrak m$ with $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak m')$ an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field] there is an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tau:R'\to R$ with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m'$. Let $R\to S$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then there are $R$-algebras $A$ and $B$ (either of which may be $0$) and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong A\times B$ such that $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-module and $R\to B$ (of finite type, $B$ being a quotient of $S$) is not quasi-finite [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at any prime ideal of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian, line 42115), proof of 8$\Rightarrow$11 (line 42224), using Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite, line 40362)

proof.text: *The etale-local decomposition (Stacks 00UK).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-etale-finite-factor-decomposition] to the finite type map $R \to S$ and the prime $\mathfrak m$. We obtain an etale ring map $R \to R'$, a prime $\mathfrak m' \subset R'$ over $\mathfrak m$ with $\kappa \cong \kappa(\mathfrak m')$, and an $R'$-algebra isomorphism $R' \otimes_R S \cong A' \times B'$, where $A'$ is finite as an $R'$-module and $R' \to B'$ is not quasi-finite at any prime over $\mathfrak m'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04GG, proof of 8 => 11, first two sentences, applying Lemma Tag 00UK

proof.text: *Retract the elementary etale extension.* The data $(R', \mathfrak m')$ from step 1 satisfy the hypothesis of the statement, so there is an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tau : R' \to R$ with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m) = \mathfrak m'$. (This corrects the reversed expression $\mathfrak m = \tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$ printed in the source, which is ill-typed.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04GG, proof of 8 => 11, sentence 'Apply (8) to get a retraction'

proof.text: *Base change the product decomposition along the retraction.* Put $A = A' \otimes_{R',\tau} R$ and $B = B' \otimes_{R',\tau} R$. Tensor cancellation gives $S \cong (R' \otimes_R S) \otimes_{R',\tau} R$, and tensor product preserves the finite product $A' \times B'$ (for two factors it is their direct sum as an $R'$-module, and the orthogonal idempotents $(1,0),(0,1)$ give the ring product after tensoring). Thus $S \cong A \times B$ as $R$-algebras. If $a'_1,\ldots,a'_n$ generate $A'$ as an $R'$-module, then $a'_1 \otimes 1,\ldots,a'_n \otimes 1$ generate $A$ as an $R$-module, so $A$ is finite. The projection $S \to B$ induced by the displayed product is surjective, hence $B$ is a quotient of the finite type $R$-algebra $S$ and is finite type over $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04GG, proof of 8 => 11, displayed tensor-product calculation; finiteness and finite type written out

proof.text: *The remaining factor has no quasi-finite point over $\mathfrak m$.* The composite $R' \xrightarrow{\tau} R \to \kappa$ has kernel $\mathfrak m' = \tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$, and the induced map $\kappa(\mathfrak m') \to \kappa$ is inverse to the isomorphism $\kappa \to \kappa(\mathfrak m')$ of step 1 (both composites are induced by the identity on $R$, hence are the identity). Tensor cancellation therefore gives an isomorphism of closed-fibre rings $B \otimes_R \kappa \cong B' \otimes_{R'} \kappa(\mathfrak m')$. Under the standard bijection between primes over the base prime and primes of the fibre ring, this isomorphism bijects primes of $B$ over $\mathfrak m$ with primes of $B'$ over $\mathfrak m'$ and is a homeomorphism on their fibre spectra. By [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], a finite type ring map is quasi-finite at such a prime exactly when its corresponding point of the fibre spectrum is isolated. Step 1 says no point on the right is isolated; hence $R \to B$ is not quasi-finite at any prime over $\mathfrak m$, as required.
